A graph structure can help by expanding the decoding space so the reranker can explore multiple paths instead of committing to one high-likelihood sequence, which reduces repetitive item lists and improves diversity [2]. In the graph-structured model in CONGRATS, item dependencies are modeled through graph transitions, and this is described as enabling more diverse sequences and avoiding the likelihood trap where repetitive sequences look high-likelihood but low-quality [2].

A related graph-based idea is to turn reranker signals into a graph structure to capture item interactions efficiently, but that paper focuses on retrieval performance rather than repetition in generated lists [1].
